conversations.title: DISABLED BUS PASS CAMPAIGN WIN ,  East Surrey News
conversations.reply: Scrapping that 9:30 am limit on bus passes makes a massive difference for morning plans. The real test now is sorting late night transport so people can stay out dancing or on dates without stressing about how to get home.

conversations.title: Every Borough of Greater Manchester Now Served by Night Buses
conversations.reply: Expanding night buses across all ten Manchester boroughs is great news for nights out. The real test is making sure working ramps and level boarding are guaranteed on every route so clubgoers can stay on the dance floor until last call.

conversations.title: Disability Advocacy Coalition 1IN4 Teams With TIFF On Film Festival Best Practices Guide ,  Read The Findings
conversations.reply: Pointing out dodgy shuttles and massive gaps between screens is spot on. Hopefully festival organisers actually put these fixes in place so everyone can just focus on enjoying the films together.

conversations.title: Manchester Cultural Welcome Award Puts Seven Venues to Public Vote
conversations.reply: Seeing seven Manchester spots shortlisted in the Cultural Welcome Award is brilliant to see. The real test is getting step-free entrances and accessible dance floors into every venue across the city so every night out is this easy.

conversations.title: Union secures £15k towards unpaid Pride performer fees
conversations.reply: Sorting £15k in unpaid fees for Canal Street performers is a massive win for everyone keeping Pride alive. What really matters next is making sure every stage has full step-free access so disabled artists can perform and celebrate alongside everyone else.

conversations.title: Seven in 10 UK Employers Lack Disability or Neurodiversity Training as Tribunal Risks Rise
conversations.reply: That seven in ten figure explains why so many people face awkward friction at work every single day. The real story is how that strain bleeds into your social life, which is why Able2Love exists to give people relaxed, understanding spaces to date.

conversations.title: Not every disability is visible. This clip explores stigma, masking ...
conversations.reply: Talking openly about the heavy toll of masking hits right at what so many people handle alone. The real shift happens when bringing up a diagnosis on a date leads to genuine understanding instead of radio silence or someone vanishing.

target_reply: Huge admiration for everything GMCDP does across Greater Manchester for accessible nightlife and transport. Able2Love would love to connect and explore ways to support your members in building welcoming, barrier-free dating and social spaces across the region.
funding: Arts Council England £1m disabled-led cultural programme grant (liverpoolexpress.co.uk). Also check UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk), and Stelios Awards (around March).
moment: September brings International Day for Universal Access to Information, but honestly, the best way to mark it is making sure venue access details are clear enough that nobody gets turned away at the pub door on a Friday night.
target: GMCDP, Greater Manchester Coalition of Disabled People (disabled-led, GM-wide members list)

instagram_hitlist.who: A Manchester disability creator posting a reel about trying to get into a local venue or club for a night out.
instagram_hitlist.why: Focuses on local Manchester nightlife and venue accessibility.
instagram_hitlist.comment: That step at the front door is frustrating enough, but the real test is whether the dance floor actually lets everyone in together. Venues with full level access show it is completely doable when nightspots choose to prioritize it.

instagram_hitlist.who: Someone posting under #disabilitydating about a match who went silent the moment disability was mentioned.
instagram_hitlist.why: Addresses the recurring pattern of disclosure vanishing on mainstream dating apps.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Having someone go quiet the second you're honest is infuriating, but standard apps have made people far too comfortable acting like that. Putting it all out there from day one is at least a brilliant filter for weeding out the wrong ones.

instagram_hitlist.who: An interabled couple sharing a reel about their date night at a music venue or festival.
instagram_hitlist.why: Celebrates genuine community connection and positive nightlife inclusion.
instagram_hitlist.comment: You two look brilliant out on the dancefloor! It just shows how great a night out is when a venue actually gets its setup right from the start.

instagram_hitlist.who: A disability community account calling out a festival or Pride event for poor wheelchair access despite inclusive marketing.
instagram_hitlist.why: Calls out superficial inclusion while holding up better standards.
instagram_hitlist.comment: It’s so frustrating when the promo promises inclusion, but you turn up and can’t even get near the stage. Organisers need to back up those posters with proper ramps and smooth paths so everyone can actually enjoy the event.

instagram_hitlist.who: A creator under #wheelchairlife sharing a post about intrusive questions and awkward tropes on mainstream dating apps.
instagram_hitlist.why: Directly touches the core reason Able2Love was built.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Having to field invasive questions before someone even says hello is so draining. Mainstream apps make it far too hard to just have a normal, straightforward chat.

instagram_hitlist.who: A creator sharing a reel about navigating diagnosis disclosure with a new partner under #invisibledisability.
instagram_hitlist.why: Grounds the reply in honest community testimony about dating and disclosure.
instagram_hitlist.comment: Opening up about a diagnosis to someone new is never easy, but the right person will just take it in their stride. Seeing people chat about this so openly makes the whole dating scene feel a lot more natural.

instagram_hitlist.who: A post under #accessibility celebrating a nightlife spot that provided step-free entry and accessible facilities for a club night.
instagram_hitlist.why: Provides a concrete positive example of nightlife inclusion.
instagram_hitlist.comment: The night is always so much better when the whole group can actually stay out together. Hopefully other venues are paying attention!

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. x_candidates.post: This matters particularly now, as disabled people are increasingly being blamed for “economic inactivity” and welfare spending. The old medical dismissal is being repackaged for a new political moment. Disabled people are not the problem. A
x_candidates.reply: Spot on. Shifting the blame onto disabled people instead of fixing broken systems is exhausting, and so many of us are completely sick of it.
